The core mathematical structure emerges from a dualism between objective pose data and subjective perception. Let F_obj ∈ ℝ^n denote an objective feature vector derived from 3D pose estimation, where each component represents a kinematic or volumetric descriptor. Let R_sub ∈ ℝ^m represent a vector of human-rated NVB dimensions. The correspondence is modeled via a linear transformation T: F_obj → R_sub, with correlation coefficient r = corr(F_obj, R_sub). This establishes a statistical isomorphism under the assumption of temporal consistency in thin-slice video segments. The breakdown regime occurs when r < 0.5 or when F_obj lacks discriminative capacity across contexts. The kinematic signature K_sig ∈ ℝ^p encodes motion dynamics, with D_dyn quantifying variability. Classification of match contexts C_ctx ∈ {−1, 0, 1} is achieved via kernel-based classifiers applied to K_sig. Ecological validity E_val ∈ [0, 1] is defined as the normalized overlap between M_obs and M_comp, where M_obs reflects human behavioral interpretation and M_comp is the computed metric. Failure modes include overfitting to lab conditions, misalignment between observer and computational models, and insufficient signal-to-noise ratio in pose data.
